fresh_source_evidence.fact: Current INSPIRE Index Polygons release is 5 July 2026 and new files are published on the first Sunday of each month.
London Borough of Lambeth is present in the current local-authority download catalogue, so candidate boundaries must resolve from that current authority file rather than a stale signed URL.
HMLR polygon geometry is captured against British National Grid and exact candidate binding must therefore remain in BNG/EPSG:27700.
BNG-to-WGS84 reprojection can shift some features by up to 15m, so reprojected coordinates are display/support evidence only and are forbidden for exact polygon identity matching.
EA LIDAR Composite DTM 1m uses EPSG:27700 and covers about 99% of England at 1m spatial resolution.
EA DTM download tiles are presented in metres referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn using OSTN15, establishing the required vertical-datum lineage for numeric parcel sampling.
The composite contains surveys from 6 June 2000 to 2 April 2022 and the metadata survey index identifies which source survey contributed at each location.

Time-stamped DTM archive metadata can report survey-specific transformation and geoidal model; historical tiles must not be mixed into the current composite numeric chain without transformation compatibility evidence.
The persistent DTM1m WCS endpoint supports WCS 2.0.1 and is intended to remain stable while serving the most up-to-date data.
EA states WMS is a summarised elevation view while WCS provides elevation coverage; numeric parcel measurements must use WCS/download raster rather than rendered WMS values.
OS Terrain50 GML expresses horizontal geometry with EPSG:27700, matching the British National Grid horizontal CRS used by the HMLR and EA source chain.
Terrain50 per-tile metadata identifies British National Grid EPSG:27700 and Ordnance Datum Newlyn EPSG:5701 as coordinate reference systems.
Terrain50 per-tile GEMINI metadata records earliest and latest flying dates, enabling temporal provenance to be retained for TQ26 and TQ27 cross-checks.

Most Terrain50 heights are relative to Ordnance Survey Newlyn Datum, while a small number of offshore islands use local datums; London candidates must therefore require Newlyn/ODN metadata and reject local-datum tiles.
Terrain50 source X/Y coordinates are Eastings/Northings in OSGB36 and Z is height in metres relative to the area datum; buildings and vegetation are excluded from the bare-earth model.
Terrain50 height property values are defined as height above Newlyn or another British height datum, so the tile metadata vertical CRS must be read before cross-source numeric comparison.
